newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP confirms Algeria exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: BHP confirms Algeria exploration deal.

text.p: Australia's The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Tuesday confirmed it had signed a production-sharing deal with Algeria's state-run oil company Sonatrach over prospective ground in the country's central east.

The agreement, first revealed on Saturday by Algeria's official APS newsagency, commits the two companies to 10 years oil and gas exploration in the Boukhechba area, west of the Tin Fouye Tabankort oil and wet gas field.
The Boukhechba area also lies just south of the Rhourde Nouss and Rhourde El Hamra oil and gas fields.
BHP's initial commitment is to drill two exploration wells, acquire 500-km of seismic data and carry out an additional 500 km of seismic reprocessing, the company said.
"The cost of this first work programme is estimated at around US$17 million," it said.
Seismic data provided by Sonatrach has already enabled BHP to identify some leads within the area, BHP said.
The exploration phase has been split into six stages, with BHP committed to spend at least US$62 million if it proceeds through all six stages, BHP spokesman Robert Porter said.

"The terms of the PSC (production-sharing contract) allow for the exploration of all forms of liquid and gaseous hydrocarbons, with BHP Petroleum responsible for 100 percent of the investment during the exploration phase," BHP said.
The contact signing follows last week's announcement by BHP that it struck oil at an exploration well in another part of the country, in the Eastern Erg region near the border with Libya.
